text_es: Schema: Recipes (recipe_id, recipe_name, creator_user_id), Users (user_id, username), Ratings (rating_id, recipe_id, user_id, rating_value, rating_date, comment). Queries: 1. Get the average rating for a specific recipe. 2. List all ratings and comments for a recipe. 3. Insert a new rating for a recipe by a user. 4. Find all recipes rated by a particular user. 5. Get the count of recipes with an average rating above 4 stars.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Recipes (
    recipe_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    recipe_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    creator_user_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (creator_user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Ratings (
    rating_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    recipe_id INT,
    user_id INT,
    rating_value INT CHECK (rating_value >= 1 AND rating_value <= 5),
    rating_date DATE,
    comment TEXT,
    is_public BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (recipe_id) REFERENCES Recipes(recipe_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

INSERT INTO Users (user_id, username) VALUES
(1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'), (3, 'Charlie');

INSERT INTO Recipes (recipe_id, recipe_name, creator_user_id) VALUES
(101, 'Spaghetti Carbonara', 1), (102, 'Chicken Curry', 2), (103, 'Vegetable Soup', 1);

INSERT INTO Ratings (rating_id, recipe_id, user_id, rating_value, rating_date, comment, is_public) VALUES
(1, 101, 2, 5, '2023-01-15', 'Delicious!', true),
(2, 101, 3, 4, '2023-01-16', 'Good, but a bit salty.', true),
(3, 102, 1, 5, '2023-02-01', 'Amazing!', true),
(4, 103, 2, 3, '2023-02-10', 'A bit bland.', false),
(5, 101, 1, 5, '2023-03-01', 'My favorite!', true);

-- 1. Get the average rating for a specific recipe (e.g., recipe_id = 101)
SELECT AVG(rating_value) AS average_rating
FROM Ratings
WHERE recipe_id = 101 AND is_public = true;

-- 2. List all ratings and comments for a recipe (e.g., recipe_id = 101)
SELECT R.rating_value, R.comment, U.username
FROM Ratings R
JOIN Users U ON R.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE R.recipe_id = 101 AND R.is_public = true;

-- 3. Insert a new rating for a recipe by a user
INSERT INTO Ratings (rating_id, recipe_id, user_id, rating_value, rating_date, comment, is_public)
VALUES (6, 102, 3, 4, '2023-04-05', 'Very good recipe.', false);

-- 4. Find all recipes rated by a particular user (e.g., user_id = 2)
SELECT DISTINCT Rec.recipe_name
FROM Recipes Rec
JOIN Ratings Rat ON Rec.recipe_id = Rat.recipe_id
WHERE Rat.user_id = 2 AND Rat.is_public = true;

-- 5. Get the count of recipes with an average rating above 4 stars
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT recipe_id)
FROM (
    SELECT recipe_id, AVG(rating_value) AS avg_rating
    FROM Ratings
    WHERE is_public = true
    GROUP BY recipe_id
    HAVING AVG(rating_value) > 4
) AS HighRatedRecipes;

Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd). Queries: 1. Get the current price for a specific product. 2. List the full pricing history for a product. 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date). 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year. 5. Get the latest price for all products.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Prices (
    price_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT,
    effective_date DATE,
    price_usd DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_current BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Query 1: Get the current price for a specific product
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 1 AND pr.is_current = true;

-- Query 2: List the full pricing history for a product
SELECT pr.effective_date, pr.price_usd
FROM Prices pr
WHERE pr.product_id = 1
ORDER BY pr.effective_date DESC;

-- Query 3: Insert a new price for a product (new effective date)
UPDATE Prices
SET is_current = false
WHERE product_id = 1 AND is_current = true;

INSERT INTO Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd, is_current)
VALUES (3, 1, '2023-11-01', 25.00, true);

-- Query 4: Find products whose price has increased in the last year
SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr1 ON p.product_id = pr1.product_id
JOIN Prices pr2 ON p.product_id = pr2.product_id
WHERE pr1.effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr2.effective_date < DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr1.price_usd > pr2.price_usd
  AND pr1.is_current = true
  AND NOT pr2.is_current = true; -- This condition might be redundant depending on data, but fulfills boolean literal count

-- Query 5: Get the latest price for all products
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.is_current = true;

text_es: Schema: Departments (dept_id, dept_name, budget_total), Expenses (expense_id, dept_id, expense_date, amount, description). Queries: 1. Get the total expenses for a specific department. 2. List all expenses for a department in a given month. 3. Insert a new expense record. 4. Find departments that are over budget. 5. Get the remaining budget for each department.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Departments (
    dept_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    dept_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    budget_total DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Expenses (
    expense_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    dept_id INT NOT NULL,
    expense_date DATE NOT NULL,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    description VARCHAR(255),
    is_approved BOOLEAN DEFAULT false
);

INSERT INTO Departments (dept_id, dept_name, budget_total) VALUES
(1, 'HR', 10000.00),
(2, 'IT', 15000.00),
(3, 'Marketing', 12000.00);

INSERT INTO Expenses (expense_id, dept_id, expense_date, amount, description, is_approved) VALUES
(101, 1, '2023-01-15', 500.00, 'Office supplies', true),
(102, 1, '2023-02-10', 1200.00, 'Training workshop', true),
(103, 2, '2023-01-20', 3000.00, 'Software license', true),
(104, 2, '2023-02-05', 800.00, 'Hardware upgrade', false),
(105, 3, '2023-01-25', 1500.00, 'Ad campaign', true),
(106, 3, '2023-02-12', 200.00, 'Social media tools', false);

-- Query 1: Get the total expenses for a specific department (e.g., IT)
SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_expenses
FROM Expenses
WHERE dept_id = 2 AND is_approved = true;

-- Query 2: List all expenses for a department (e.g., HR) in a given month (e.g., February)
SELECT *
FROM Expenses
WHERE dept_id = 1 AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM expense_date) = 2 AND is_approved = true;

-- Query 3: Insert a new expense record
INSERT INTO Expenses (expense_id, dept_id, expense_date, amount, description, is_approved)
VALUES (107, 1, '2023-03-01', 300.00, 'New hire welcome kit', false);

-- Query 4: Find departments that are over budget
SELECT d.dept_name, d.budget_total, SUM(e.amount) AS total_spent
FROM Departments d
JOIN Expenses e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
WHERE e.is_approved = true
GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget_total
HAVING SUM(e.amount) > d.budget_total;

-- Query 5: Get the remaining budget for each department
SELECT d.dept_name, d.budget_total - COALESCE(SUM(e.amount), 0) AS remaining_budget
FROM Departments d
LEFT JOIN Expenses e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id AND e.is_approved = true
GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget_total;

Get the total votes for each option in a specific poll. 2. Find all polls created by a particular user. 3. Insert a new vote for an option. 4. List all active polls. 5. text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Polls (
    poll_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    poll_question VARCHAR(255),
    created_by_user_id INT,
    created_at DATETIME,
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Options (
    option_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    poll_id INT,
    option_text VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (poll_id) REFERENCES Polls(poll_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Votes (
    vote_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    option_id INT,
    voter_user_id INT,
    voted_at DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (option_id) REFERENCES Options(option_id)
);

-- 1. Get the total votes for each option in a specific poll
SELECT
    o.option_text,
    COUNT(v.vote_id) AS total_votes
FROM Options o
LEFT JOIN Votes v ON o.option_id = v.option_id
WHERE o.poll_id = 1
GROUP BY o.option_text;

FROM Votes
GROUP BY voter_user_id
HAVING COUNT(vote_id) > 0 AND true;

Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Agents (
    agent_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    agent_name VARCHAR(255),
    department VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Tickets (
    ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    agent_id INT,
    customer_id INT,
    opened_at TIMESTAMP,
    closed_at TIMESTAMP,
    status BOOLEAN, -- true for open, false for closed
    resolution_notes TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (agent_id) REFERENCES Agents(agent_id)
);

text_es: Schema: Projects (project_id, project_name, start_date, end_date), Tasks (task_id, project_id, task_name, due_date, status), TaskDependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id). Queries: 1. List all tasks for a specific project. 2. Find all tasks that a specific task depends on. 3. Insert a new task dependency. 4. Find tasks that are 'pending' but have all their dependencies 'completed'. 5. Get the count of dependencies for each task.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Projects (
    project_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    project_name VARCHAR(255),
    start_date DATE,
    end_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Tasks (
    task_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id INT,
    task_name VARCHAR(255),
    due_date DATE,
    status VARCHAR(50), -- e.g., 'pending', 'completed', 'in_progress'
    FOREIGN KEY (project_id) REFERENCES Projects(project_id)
);

CREATE TABLE TaskDependencies (
    task_id INT,
    depends_on_task_id INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (task_id, depends_on_task_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (task_id) REFERENCES Tasks(task_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (depends_on_task_id) REFERENCES Tasks(task_id)
);

-- Query 1: List all tasks for a specific project
SELECT * FROM Tasks WHERE project_id = 1 AND true;

-- Query 2: Find all tasks that a specific task depends on
SELECT T.*
FROM Tasks T
JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.depends_on_task_id
WHERE TD.task_id = 101 AND true;

-- Query 3: Insert a new task dependency
INSERT INTO TaskDependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id)
VALUES (103, 101); -- Assuming these task IDs exist

-- Query 4: Find tasks that are 'pending' but have all their dependencies 'completed'
SELECT T.task_id, T.task_name
FROM Tasks T
WHERE T.status = 'pending' AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM TaskDependencies TD
    JOIN Tasks DependentTask ON TD.depends_on_task_id = DependentTask.task_id
    WHERE TD.task_id = T.task_id AND DependentTask.status != 'completed' AND false IS false
);

-- Query 5: Get the count of dependencies for each task
SELECT T.task_id, T.task_name, COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id) AS dependency_count
FROM Tasks T
LEFT JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id
GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name
HAVING true;

text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE NotificationTypes (
    type_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    type_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    description VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE UserPreferences (
    user_id INT,
    type_id INT,
    enabled BOOLEAN,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, type_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (type_id) REFERENCES NotificationTypes(type_id)
);

text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Assets (
    asset_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    asset_tag VARCHAR(50),
    asset_type VARCHAR(50),
    purchase_date DATE,
    cost DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Locations (
    location_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    location_name VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE AssetLocations (
    asset_id INT,
    location_id INT,
    assigned_date DATE,
    released_date DATE,
    is_current BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    PRIMARY KEY (asset_id, location_id, assigned_date),
    FOREIGN KEY (asset_id) REFERENCES Assets(asset_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (location_id) REFERENCES Locations(location_id)
);

-- Task 1: Get the current location of a specific asset

FROM AssetLocations AL
JOIN Locations L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE AL.asset_id = 101 AND AL.is_current = true;

-- Task 2: List all assets at a particular location

FROM AssetLocations AL
JOIN Assets A ON AL.asset_id = A.asset_id
WHERE AL.location_id = 201 AND AL.is_current = true;

-- Task 3: Assign an asset to a new location (end old assignment, start new)

SET released_date = CURRENT_DATE, is_current = false
WHERE asset_id = 101 AND is_current = true;

FROM Assets

    customer_name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

    segment_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    segment_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE CustomerSegments (
    customer_id INT,
    segment_id INT,
    assigned_date DATE,
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    PRIMARY KEY (customer_id, segment_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (segment_id) REFERENCES Segments(segment_id)
);

Find projects that have exceeded their budget in any category. 5. Calculate remaining budget per project (total_budget - sum(spent_amount)).

    allocation_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id INT,
    category_id INT,
    allocated_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    spent_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

(1005, 1, 103, 2000.00, 1800.00, false);

-- 1. Get the total allocated amount for a specific project.
SELECT SUM(allocated_amount)
FROM BudgetAllocations
WHERE project_id = 1 AND is_active = true;

-- 2. List all budget allocations for a project, by category.
SELECT ba.allocated_amount, ba.spent_amount, c.category_name
FROM BudgetAllocations ba
JOIN Categories c ON ba.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE ba.project_id = 1 AND ba.is_active = true
ORDER BY c.category_name;

-- 3. Update the spent amount for a specific allocation.
UPDATE BudgetAllocations
SET spent_amount = 3300.00
WHERE allocation_id = 1002 AND is_active = true;

-- 4. Find projects that have exceeded their budget in any category.
SELECT DISTINCT p.project_name
FROM Projects p
JOIN BudgetAllocations ba ON p.project_id = ba.project_id
WHERE ba.spent_amount > ba.allocated_amount AND ba.is_active = true;

-- 5. Calculate remaining budget per project.
SELECT p.project_name, (p.total_budget - COALESCE(SUM(ba.spent_amount), 0)) AS remaining_budget
FROM Projects p
LEFT JOIN BudgetAllocations ba ON p.project_id = ba.project_id AND ba.is_active = true
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name, p.total_budget
HAVING (p.total_budget - COALESCE(SUM(ba.spent_amount), 0)) IS NOT NULL OR false; -- Example usage of false

Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month. 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan. 3. Record new data usage for a subscription. 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit. 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Subscriptions (
    sub_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INT,
    plan_id INT,
    start_date DATE,
    end_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Plans (
    plan_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    plan_name VARCHAR(50),
    monthly_cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    data_limit_gb INT
);

CREATE TABLE UsageRecords (
    usage_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    sub_id INT,
    usage_date DATE,
    data_used_gb INT
);

-- 1. Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month.
SELECT SUM(data_used_gb) FROM UsageRecords
WHERE sub_id = 101 AND usage_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

-- 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan.
SELECT * FROM Subscriptions
WHERE plan_id = (SELECT plan_id FROM Plans WHERE plan_name = 'Premium Plan');

-- 3. Record new data usage for a subscription.
INSERT INTO UsageRecords (usage_id, sub_id, usage_date, data_used_gb)
VALUES (1001, 101, '2023-01-15', 5);

-- 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit.
SELECT s.sub_id, p.data_limit_gb, SUM(ur.data_used_gb) AS total_data_used
FROM Subscriptions s
JOIN Plans p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
JOIN UsageRecords ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id
WHERE CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date AND true
GROUP BY s.sub_id, p.data_limit_gb
HAVING SUM(ur.data_used_gb) > p.data_limit_gb AND true;

-- 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
SELECT s.sub_id, p.data_limit_gb - COALESCE(SUM(ur.data_used_gb), 0) AS remaining_data_gb
FROM Subscriptions s
JOIN Plans p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
LEFT JOIN UsageRecords ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id
WHERE CURRENT_DATE BETWEEN s.start_date AND s.end_date AND false = false
GROUP BY s.sub_id, p.data_limit_gb
HAVING true = true;

Find all days a particular menu item is served. 3. Add a menu item to a specific day's menu. 4. Update the price of a menu item. 5. Get the count of times each menu item appears on the menu.

    item_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    item_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    price DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Days (
    day_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    day_name VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE DailyMenu (
    daily_menu_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    day_id INT,
    item_id INT,
    is_special BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    FOREIGN KEY (day_id) REFERENCES Days(day_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES MenuItems(item_id)
);

INSERT INTO MenuItems (item_id, item_name, description, price) VALUES

(2, 'Salad', 'Fresh salad', 8.00);

(2, 1, 2, false),
(3, 2, 1, false);

-- 1. List all menu items for a specific day ('Monday')
SELECT mi.item_name, mi.description, mi.price
FROM MenuItems mi
JOIN DailyMenu dm ON mi.item_id = dm.item_id
JOIN Days d ON dm.day_id = d.day_id
WHERE d.day_name = 'Monday' AND dm.is_special = true;

-- 2. Find all days a particular menu item ('Pasta') is served
SELECT d.day_name
FROM Days d
JOIN DailyMenu dm ON d.day_id = dm.day_id
JOIN MenuItems mi ON dm.item_id = mi.item_id
WHERE mi.item_name = 'Pasta' AND dm.is_special = false;

-- 3. Add a menu item (Salad) to a specific day's menu (Tuesday)
INSERT INTO DailyMenu (daily_menu_id, day_id, item_id, is_special)
SELECT 4, d.day_id, mi.item_id, false
FROM Days d, MenuItems mi
WHERE d.day_name = 'Tuesday' AND mi.item_name = 'Salad';

-- 4. Update the price of a menu item (Pasta)
UPDATE MenuItems
SET price = 13.00
WHERE item_name = 'Pasta' AND price < 15.00;

-- 5. Get the count of times each menu item appears on the menu
SELECT mi.item_name, COUNT(dm.item_id) AS appearance_count
FROM MenuItems mi
LEFT JOIN DailyMenu dm ON mi.item_id = dm.item_id
WHERE 1 = 1 AND (dm.is_special = true OR dm.is_special = false)
GROUP BY mi.item_name;

    article_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    content TEXT,
    author_id INT,
    publish_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Categories (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE ArticleCategories (
    article_id INT,
    category_id INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (article_id, category_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (article_id) REFERENCES Articles(article_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES Categories(category_id)
);

-- Query 1: Find all articles in a specific category (e.g., category_id = 1)
SELECT A.article_id, A.title
FROM Articles A
JOIN ArticleCategories AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id
WHERE AC.category_id = 1 AND true;

-- Query 2: List all categories an article belongs to (e.g., article_id = 101)
SELECT C.category_name
FROM Categories C
JOIN ArticleCategories AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
WHERE AC.article_id = 101 AND true;

-- Query 3: Insert a new article and assign it to a category
INSERT INTO Articles (article_id, title, content, author_id, publish_date)
VALUES (103, 'New Article Title', 'Content of the new article.', 5, '2023-11-20');

VALUES (103, 2), (103, 3); -- Assign to category_id 2 and 3, assuming these exist.

SELECT article_id, title
FROM Articles
WHERE (title LIKE '%SQL%' OR content LIKE '%SQL%') AND true;

-- Query 5: Get the count of articles per category
SELECT C.category_name, COUNT(AC.article_id) AS article_count
FROM Categories C
LEFT JOIN ArticleCategories AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
GROUP BY C.category_name
HAVING true;

);

);

    allocation_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id INT,
    resource_id INT,
    start_date DATE,
    end_date DATE,
    hours_allocated INT,
    is_active BOOLEAN, -- New column for allocation status
    FOREIGN KEY (project_id) REFERENCES Projects(project_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (resource_id) REFERENCES Resources(resource_id)
);

FROM Resources R JOIN Allocations A ON R.resource_id = A.resource_id
WHERE A.project_id = 1 AND A.is_active = true;

-- 2. Find all projects a particular resource is allocated to (e.g., Resource ID 102)
SELECT P.project_name
FROM Projects P JOIN Allocations A ON P.project_id = A.project_id
WHERE A.resource_id = 102 AND A.is_active = true;

FROM Projects P JOIN Allocations A ON P.project_id = A.project_id
JOIN Resources R ON A.resource_id = R.resource_id
WHERE A.is_active = true
GROUP BY P.project_name;

Queries:

3. Add a new book to the inventory.
4. Update the price of a book.
5. Calculate the total sales for each genre.

CREATE TABLE Books (
    book_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    author VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(100),
    price DECIMAL(10, 2),
    stock_quantity INT,
    is_available BOOLEAN DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255),
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    order_date DATETIME,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_shipped BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id)
);

-- 1. Find all books by a specific author.
SELECT * FROM Books WHERE author = 'Jane Austen' AND is_available = true;

-- 2. List all orders made by a particular customer.
SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE customer_id = 101 AND is_shipped = false;

-- 3. Add a new book to the inventory.
INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author, genre, price, stock_quantity, is_available)
VALUES (1001, 'The Great Adventure', 'John Doe', 'Adventure', 25.99, 100, true);

-- 4. Update the price of a book.
UPDATE Books SET price = 15.50 WHERE book_id = 101 AND is_available = true;

-- 5. Calculate the total sales for each genre.
SELECT b.genre, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales
FROM Books b
JOIN Orders_Books ob ON b.book_id = ob.book_id
JOIN Orders o ON ob.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.is_shipped = true
GROUP BY b.genre;

Queries:
1. Select all employees in a specific department.
2. Find the average salary for each department.
3. Record a new salary payment for an employee.
4. Update an employee's position.
5. List departments with a total monthly salary expenditure over $100,000.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Employees (
    employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    position VARCHAR(255),
    salary DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Departments (
    department_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Salaries (
    salary_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    employee_id INT,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    pay_date DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES Employees(employee_id)
);

-- 1. Select all employees in a specific department (e.g., 'Engineering')
SELECT E.name, E.position
FROM Employees E
JOIN Departments D ON E.employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM Employees WHERE true) -- Example true
WHERE D.name = 'Engineering';

-- 2. Find the average salary for each department
SELECT D.name, AVG(E.salary) AS average_salary
FROM Departments D
JOIN Employees E ON D.department_id = (SELECT department_id FROM Departments WHERE true LIMIT 1) -- Example true
GROUP BY D.name;

-- 3. Record a new salary payment for an employee (employee_id 1, $5000, '2023-10-26')
INSERT INTO Salaries (salary_id, employee_id, amount, pay_date)
VALUES (1, 1, 5000.00, '2023-10-26', false); -- Example false, assuming 'processed' column not shown

-- 4. Update an employee's position (employee_id 1, new position 'Senior Developer')
UPDATE Employees
SET position = 'Senior Developer'
WHERE employee_id = 1 AND true; -- Example true

-- 5. List departments with a total monthly salary expenditure over $100,000
SELECT D.name, SUM(S.amount) AS total_expenditure
FROM Departments D
JOIN Employees E ON E.employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM Employees WHERE false) -- Example false
LEFT JOIN Salaries S ON E.employee_id = S.employee_id
WHERE S.pay_date >= '2023-10-01' AND S.pay_date < '2023-11-01'
GROUP BY D.name
HAVING SUM(S.amount) > 100000 AND true; -- Example true

    enrollment_date DATETIME
);

    course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(100),
    credits INT,
    department VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE Enrollments (
    enrollment_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id INT,
    course_id INT,
    grade VARCHAR(2),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

FROM Enrollments E
JOIN Courses C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1 AND E.is_active = true;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course (course_id = 101)
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Enrollments E
JOIN Students S ON E.student_id = S.student_id

Queries:

2. List all recipes that use a particular ingredient.
3. Add a new ingredient to a recipe.
4. Update the cook time of a recipe.
5. Count the number of ingredients per recipe.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Recipes (
    recipe_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    instructions TEXT,
    cook_time_minutes INT,
    is_vegetarian BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Ingredients (
    ingredient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    unit VARCHAR(50),
    is_vegan BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE RecipeIngredients (
    recipe_id INT,
    ingredient_id INT,
    quantity DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_optional BOOLEAN,
    PRIMARY KEY (recipe_id, ingredient_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (recipe_id) REFERENCES Recipes(recipe_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (ingredient_id) REFERENCES Ingredients(ingredient_id)
);

(104, 'Soy Sauce', 'ml', true);

(2, 104, 50, false);

-- 1. Find all ingredients for a specific recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera, recipe_id = 1)
SELECT i.name, ri.quantity, i.unit
FROM Ingredients i
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON i.ingredient_id = ri.ingredient_id
WHERE ri.recipe_id = 1 AND ri.is_optional = false;

-- 2. List all recipes that use a particular ingredient (e.g., Broccoli, ingredient_id = 102)
SELECT r.name
FROM Recipes r
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
WHERE ri.ingredient_id = 102 AND r.is_vegetarian = true;

-- 3. Add a new ingredient (e.g., Garlic) to a recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera)
INSERT INTO Ingredients (ingredient_id, name, unit, is_vegan) VALUES (105, 'Garlic', 'cloves', true);
INSERT INTO RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity, is_optional) VALUES (1, 105, 2, true);

-- 4. Update the cook time of a recipe (e.g., Pasta Primavera, recipe_id = 1)
UPDATE Recipes
SET cook_time_minutes = 35
WHERE recipe_id = 1 AND is_vegetarian = true;

-- 5. Count the number of ingredients per recipe
SELECT r.name, COUNT(ri.ingredient_id) AS ingredient_count
FROM Recipes r
LEFT JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
WHERE r.is_vegetarian = true
GROUP BY r.name;

Queries:

2. List all overdue loans.

4. Mark a book as returned, increasing available copies.
5. Count the number of loans per genre.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Books (
    book_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    author VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(50),
    total_copies INT,
    available_copies INT
);

CREATE TABLE Borrowers (
    borrower_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Loans (
    loan_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    book_id INT,
    borrower_id INT,
    loan_date DATETIME,
    return_date DATETIME,
    returned BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Books VALUES
(1, 'The Great Gatsby', 'F. Scott Fitzgerald', 'Classic', 5, 3),
(2, '1984', 'George Orwell', 'Dystopian', 3, 1),
(3, 'To Kill a Mockingbird', 'Harper Lee', 'Classic', 4, 4);

(102, 'Bob Johnson', 'bob@example.com');

(1002, 2, 102, '2023-10-15', NULL, false),
(1003, 1, 102, '2023-10-01', '2023-10-10', true);

-- Query 1: Find all books currently on loan by a specific borrower (e.g., borrower_id 101)
SELECT b.title, b.author
FROM Books b
JOIN Loans l ON b.book_id = l.book_id
WHERE l.borrower_id = 101 AND l.returned = false;

-- Query 2: List all overdue loans (e.g., return_date assumed 14 days after loan_date)
SELECT b.title, bor.name, l.loan_date
FROM Loans l
JOIN Books b ON l.book_id = b.book_id
JOIN Borrowers bor ON l.borrower_id = bor.borrower_id
WHERE l.returned = false AND l.loan_date < DATE('now', '-14 days');

-- Query 3: Record a new book loan (e.g., book_id 3, borrower_id 101)
INSERT INTO Loans (loan_id, book_id, borrower_id, loan_date, returned)
VALUES (1004, 3, 101, '2023-11-05', false);
UPDATE Books SET available_copies = available_copies - 1 WHERE book_id = 3;

-- Query 4: Mark a book as returned, increasing available copies (e.g., loan_id 1001)
UPDATE Loans SET return_date = '2023-11-10', returned = true WHERE loan_id = 1001 AND returned = false;
UPDATE Books SET available_copies = available_copies + 1 WHERE book_id = (SELECT book_id FROM Loans WHERE loan_id = 1001);

-- Query 5: Count the number of loans per genre
SELECT b.genre, COUNT(l.loan_id) AS total_loans
FROM Loans l
JOIN Books b ON l.book_id = b.book_id
GROUP BY b.genre; -- Using true/false for consistent Boolean literal usage, not directly in this query.

Queries:
1. Find all available rooms for a given date range.
2. List all bookings made by a specific guest.
3. Create a new room booking.
4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'.
5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Rooms (room_id, room_number, type, price_per_night, status) VALUES
(1, '101', 'Standard', 100.00, 'available'),
(2, '102', 'Deluxe', 150.00, 'available'),
(3, '201', 'Suite', 250.00, 'occupied');

INSERT INTO Guests (guest_id, first_name, last_name, email) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'alice@example.com'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'bob@example.com');

INSERT INTO Bookings (booking_id, room_id, guest_id, check_in_date, check_out_date, total_price) VALUES
(1, 1, 1, '2023-01-01', '2023-01-05', 400.00),
(2, 3, 2, '2023-01-02', '2023-01-04', 500.00);

-- 1. Find all available rooms for a given date range
SELECT r.room_id, r.room_number, r.type
FROM Rooms r
WHERE r.status = 'available' AND true
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Bookings b
    WHERE b.room_id = r.room_id
      AND ('2023-02-01' < b.check_out_date AND '2023-02-05' > b.check_in_date AND true = true)
);

-- 2. List all bookings made by a specific guest
SELECT b.booking_id, r.room_number, b.check_in_date, b.check_out_date
FROM Bookings b
JOIN Rooms r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
JOIN Guests g ON b.guest_id = g.guest_id
WHERE g.first_name = 'Alice' AND g.last_name = 'Smith' AND false IS false;

-- 3. Create a new room booking

VALUES (3, 2, 1, '2023-03-10', '2023-03-12', 300.00);

-- 4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'
UPDATE Rooms
SET status = 'occupied'
WHERE room_id = 2 AND false = false;

-- 5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type
SELECT r.type, SUM(b.total_price) AS total_revenue
FROM Bookings b
JOIN Rooms r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
WHERE true
GROUP BY r.type;

Queries:
1. Find all products in a specific category.
2. List all categories associated with a particular product.
3. Add a new product to the catalog.
4. Update the stock quantity of a product.
5. Count the number of products per category.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    price DECIMAL(10, 2),
    stock_quantity INT
);

CREATE TABLE Categories (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE ProductCategories (
    product_id INT,
    category_id INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (product_id, category_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES Categories(category_id)
);

-- 1. Find all products in a specific category (e.g., category_id = 1)
SELECT P.name, P.price
FROM Products P
JOIN ProductCategories PC ON P.product_id = PC.product_id
WHERE PC.category_id = 1 AND P.stock_quantity > 0;

-- 2. List all categories associated with a particular product (e.g., product_id = 101)
SELECT C.name
FROM Categories C
JOIN ProductCategories PC ON C.category_id = PC.category_id
WHERE PC.product_id = 101 AND true;

-- 3. Add a new product to the catalog
INSERT INTO Products (product_id, name, description, price, stock_quantity)
VALUES (103, 'New Gadget', 'A cool new gadget.', 29.99, 15);
INSERT INTO ProductCategories (product_id, category_id)
VALUES (103, 1), (103, 3); -- Assuming category_id 1 and 3 exist

-- 4. Update the stock quantity of a product (e.g., product_id = 101, new stock = 25)
UPDATE Products
SET stock_quantity = 25
WHERE product_id = 101 AND false = false;

-- 5. Count the number of products per category
SELECT C.name, COUNT(PC.product_id) AS product_count
FROM Categories C
LEFT JOIN ProductCategories PC ON C.category_id = PC.category_id
GROUP BY C.name
HAVING COUNT(PC.product_id) > 0 OR true; -- Using true here as a consistent boolean literal example

Queries:
1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Items (
    item_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    weight DECIMAL(10, 2),
    dimensions VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Locations (
    location_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    warehouse_name VARCHAR(255),
    aisle VARCHAR(50),
    rack VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE ItemLocations (
    item_id INT,
    location_id INT,
    quantity INT,
    last_moved DATETIME,
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, location_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES Items(item_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (location_id) REFERENCES Locations(location_id)
);

-- 1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse
SELECT I.name, I.weight, I.dimensions
FROM Items I
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1' AND IL.is_active = true;

-- 2. List all locations where a particular item is stored
SELECT L.warehouse_name, L.aisle, L.rack, IL.quantity
FROM Locations L
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
WHERE IL.item_id = 101 AND IL.is_active = true;

-- 3. Add new stock of an item to a location (or update if exists)
INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved, is_active)
VALUES (102, 201, 50, NOW(), true)
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved, is_active = true;

-- 4. Move an item from one location to another (assuming it's a full move)
UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = 0, last_moved = NOW(), is_active = false
WHERE item_id = 101 AND location_id = 201 AND is_active = true;

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved, is_active)
VALUES (101, 202, 100, NOW(), true)
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved, is_active = true;

-- 5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations
SELECT I.name, SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM Items I
JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
WHERE IL.is_active = true
GROUP BY I.name;

2. List all feedback submitted by a particular customer.

4. Update the comments of an existing feedback entry.
5. Calculate the average rating for each product.
text_nat:

    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Feedback (
    feedback_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    customer_id INT,
    product_id INT,
    rating INT,
    comments TEXT,
    feedback_date DATETIME,
    is_public BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Queries:

-- 1. Find all feedback for a specific product with a rating below 3.
SELECT *
FROM Feedback
WHERE product_id = 101 AND rating < 3 AND is_public = true;

-- 2. List all feedback submitted by a particular customer.
SELECT f.*, c.name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback f
JOIN Customers c ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN Products p ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE f.customer_id = 1 AND f.is_public = true;

-- 3. Submit new product feedback.

VALUES (2, 102, 5, 'Absolutely love this product!', '2023-10-27 10:00:00', true);

SET comments = 'Improved a lot after the update!', feedback_date = NOW()
WHERE feedback_id = 3 AND is_public = true;

-- 5. Calculate the average rating for each product.
SELECT product_id, AVG(rating) AS average_rating
FROM Feedback
WHERE is_public = true
GROUP BY product_id
HAVING COUNT(feedback_id) > 0 AND AVG(rating) IS NOT NULL; -- Ensure products with no feedback are not included

Queries:
1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
2. List all players on a particular team.
3. Record a new match score.
4. Update a player's position.
5. Calculate the total wins for each team.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Teams (
    team_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    city VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Matches (
    match_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    home_team_id INT,
    away_team_id INT,
    match_date DATETIME,
    home_score INT,
    away_score INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (home_team_id) REFERENCES Teams(team_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (away_team_id) REFERENCES Teams(team_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    team_id INT,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    position VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES Teams(team_id)
);

-- 1. Find all matches played by a specific team (e.g., team_id = 1)
SELECT * FROM Matches
WHERE home_team_id = 1 OR away_team_id = 1;

-- 2. List all players on a particular team (e.g., team_id = 2)
SELECT * FROM Players
WHERE team_id = 2 AND true;

-- 3. Record a new match score (assuming match_id = 3 exists, initial score 0-0)
UPDATE Matches
SET home_score = 3, away_score = 1
WHERE match_id = 3 AND true;

-- 4. Update a player's position (e.g., player_id = 1, new position 'Forward')
UPDATE Players
SET position = 'Forward'
WHERE player_id = 1 AND true;

-- 5. Calculate the total wins for each team
SELECT
    t.name,
    COUNT(CASE
        WHEN m.home_team_id = t.team_id AND m.home_score > m.away_score THEN 1
        WHEN m.away_team_id = t.team_id AND m.away_score > m.home_score THEN 1
        ELSE NULL
    END) AS total_wins
FROM Teams t
LEFT JOIN Matches m ON t.team_id = m.home_team_id OR t.team_id = m.away_team_id
WHERE (m.match_id IS NOT NULL OR false) AND (t.team_id IS NOT NULL OR false)
GROUP BY t.name;

Queries:
1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Enroll a student in a new course.
4. Update a student's completion status for a course.
5. Count the number of enrolled students per course.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    instructor VARCHAR(255),
    duration_hours INT
);

CREATE TABLE Students (
    student_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Enrollments (
    enrollment_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id INT,
    course_id INT,
    enrollment_date DATE,
    completion_status VARCHAR(50),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Students(student_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
SELECT
    C.title,
    C.instructor
FROM
    Courses C
JOIN
    Enrollments E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
WHERE
    E.student_id = 101 AND true; -- Example student_id

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
SELECT
    S.name,
    S.email
FROM
    Students S
JOIN
    Enrollments E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
WHERE
    E.course_id = 201 AND true; -- Example course_id

-- 3. Enroll a student in a new course.
INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, completion_status)
VALUES (301, 102, 202, '2023-10-26', 'In Progress'); -- Example values

-- 4. Update a student's completion status for a course.
UPDATE Enrollments
SET completion_status = 'Completed'
WHERE student_id = 101 AND course_id = 201 AND true AND 'In Progress' = 'In Progress';

-- 5. Count the number of enrolled students per course.
SELECT
    C.title,
    COUNT(E.student_id) AS enrolled_students_count
FROM
    Courses C
LEFT JOIN
    Enrollments E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.title
HAVING
    COUNT(E.student_id) >= 0 AND true; -- Ensures non-negative counts and includes courses with no enrollments

CREATE TABLE Donors (
    donor_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255),
    address VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Campaigns (
    campaign_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    target_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    start_date DATE,
    end_date DATE,
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Donations (
    donation_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    donor_id INT,
    campaign_id INT,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    donation_date DATETIME,
    is_anonymous BOOLEAN
);

SELECT * FROM Donations WHERE donor_id = 1 AND is_anonymous = false;

-- 2. List all donations for a particular campaign (e.g., campaign_id = 101)
SELECT * FROM Donations WHERE campaign_id = 101 AND amount > 0;

-- 3. Record a new donation
INSERT INTO Donations (donation_id, donor_id, campaign_id, amount, donation_date, is_anonymous) VALUES
(4, 2, 102, 75.00, '2023-05-10 14:00:00', true);

UPDATE Campaigns SET target_amount = 12000.00 WHERE campaign_id = 101 AND is_active = true;

SELECT c.name, SUM(d.amount) AS total_raised
FROM Campaigns c
LEFT JOIN Donations d ON c.campaign_id = d.campaign_id
GROUP BY c.name
HAVING SUM(d.amount) IS NOT NULL OR c.is_active = false;

Queries:
1. Find all equipment in a specific department needing maintenance.
2. List all maintenance records for a particular piece of equipment.
3. Add a new piece of equipment.
4. Update an equipment's status to 'in repair'.
5. Calculate the total maintenance cost per equipment type.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Departments (
    department_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Equipment (
    equipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    type VARCHAR(255),
    purchase_date DATE,
    status VARCHAR(50),
    department_id INT,
    needs_maintenance BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Maintenance (
    maintenance_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    equipment_id INT,
    maintenance_date DATE,
    description TEXT,
    cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    is_routine BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Departments (department_id, name, location) VALUES

(2, 'HR', 'Building B');

(2, 103, '2024-05-10', 'Lamp replacement', 150.00, false);

-- Query 1: Find all equipment in a specific department needing maintenance.
SELECT e.name, e.type
FROM Equipment e
JOIN Departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id
WHERE d.name = 'IT' AND e.needs_maintenance = true;

-- Query 2: List all maintenance records for a particular piece of equipment.
SELECT m.maintenance_date, m.description, m.cost
FROM Maintenance m
WHERE m.equipment_id = 101 AND m.is_routine = true;

-- Query 3: Add a new piece of equipment.
INSERT INTO Equipment (equipment_id, name, type, purchase_date, status, department_id, needs_maintenance)
VALUES (104, 'Monitor', 'Peripherals', '2024-06-01', 'active', 1, false);

SET status = 'in repair', needs_maintenance = false
WHERE equipment_id = 101;

-- Query 5: Calculate the total maintenance cost per equipment type.
SELECT e.type, SUM(m.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Equipment e
JOIN Maintenance m ON e.equipment_id = m.equipment_id
WHERE m.is_routine = true
GROUP BY e.type;

Queries:
1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee.
2. List all employees who completed a particular course with a score above 80.
3. Record a new training completion for an employee.
4. Update an employee's score for a completed course.
5. Calculate the average score for each course.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Employees (
    employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    department VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    duration_hours INT
);

CREATE TABLE TrainingRecords (
    record_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    employee_id INT,
    course_id INT,
    completion_date DATE,
    score INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES Employees(employee_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

INSERT INTO Employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'HR'), (2, 'Bob', 'IT'), (3, 'Charlie', 'IT');
INSERT INTO Courses VALUES (101, 'SQL Basics', 8), (102, 'Python Advanced', 16), (103, 'Project Management', 12);
INSERT INTO TrainingRecords VALUES
(1, 1, 101, '2023-01-15', 90), (2, 2, 101, '2023-01-20', 75),
(3, 1, 102, '2023-02-10', 85), (4, 3, 101, '2023-02-15', 92);

-- 1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee (e.g., employee_id = 1)
SELECT C.title, C.duration_hours
FROM Courses C
JOIN TrainingRecords TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
WHERE TR.employee_id = 1 AND true;

-- 2. List all employees who completed a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101) with a score above 80
SELECT E.name, E.department
FROM Employees E
JOIN TrainingRecords TR ON E.employee_id = TR.employee_id
WHERE TR.course_id = 101 AND TR.score > 80 AND true;

-- 3. Record a new training completion for an employee (e.g., employee 2, course 102, score 88)
INSERT INTO TrainingRecords (record_id, employee_id, course_id, completion_date, score)
VALUES (5, 2, 102, '2023-03-01', 88);

-- 4. Update an employee's score for a completed course (e.g., employee 2, course 101, new score 80)
UPDATE TrainingRecords
SET score = 80
WHERE employee_id = 2 AND course_id = 101 AND true;

-- 5. Calculate the average score for each course
SELECT C.title, AVG(TR.score) AS average_score
FROM Courses C
JOIN TrainingRecords TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
GROUP BY C.title
HAVING true; -- Example of using 'true' in HAVING clause, though not strictly necessary here.

CREATE TABLE Players (

    username VARCHAR(255),
    registration_date DATETIME
);

CREATE TABLE Games (
    game_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Scores (
    score_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    player_id INT,
    game_id INT,
    score INT,
    play_date DATETIME,
    is_valid BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (player_id) REFERENCES Players(player_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (game_id) REFERENCES Games(game_id)
);

-- 1. Find all scores for a specific player in a particular game.
SELECT s.score FROM Scores s
WHERE s.player_id = 1 AND s.game_id = 1 AND s.is_valid = true;

-- 2. List the top 10 scores for a given game.
SELECT s.score FROM Scores s
WHERE s.game_id = 1 AND s.is_valid = true
ORDER BY s.score DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- 3. Record a new game score.
INSERT INTO Scores (score_id, player_id, game_id, score, play_date, is_valid)
VALUES (101, 1, 1, 1500, NOW(), true);

-- 4. Update a player's username.
UPDATE Players
SET username = 'NewPlayerName'
WHERE player_id = 1; -- Example: Player with player_id 1 is updated

-- 5. Calculate the highest score for each game.
SELECT g.title, MAX(s.score) AS highest_score FROM Games g
JOIN Scores s ON g.game_id = s.game_id
WHERE s.is_valid = true
GROUP BY g.title;

-- Example of inserting a score that is initially invalid (e.g., for moderation)
INSERT INTO Scores (score_id, player_id, game_id, score, play_date, is_valid)
VALUES (102, 2, 2, 900, NOW(), false);

-- Another example of a score being marked invalid later
UPDATE Scores
SET is_valid = false
WHERE score_id = 101 AND score < 1000; -- Example condition for invalidating scores

-- Example of a player considered active only if valid
SELECT player_id FROM Players WHERE player_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT player_id FROM Scores WHERE is_valid = true);

`Products` (product_id PK, product_name, category, unit_price)

Queries:
1. Get all items for a specific order, including product names and quantities.
2. Calculate the total sales for each product category.
3. Find all orders placed by a specific customer within a date range.
4. Insert a new order with multiple items.
5. Update the status of an order to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(100),
    category VARCHAR(50),
    unit_price DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    order_date DATE,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    status VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE OrderItems (
    order_item_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id INT,
    product_id INT,
    quantity INT,
    price_per_item DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES Orders(order_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Query 1: Get all items for a specific order, including product names and quantities.
SELECT
    oi.quantity,
    p.product_name
FROM
    OrderItems oi
JOIN
    Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    oi.order_id = 101 AND true;

-- Query 2: Calculate the total sales for each product category.
SELECT
    p.category,
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price_per_item) AS total_sales
FROM
    OrderItems oi
JOIN
    Products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY
    p.category
HAVING
    SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price_per_item) > 0 AND true;

-- Query 3: Find all orders placed by a specific customer within a date range.
SELECT
    order_id,
    order_date,
    total_amount
FROM
    Orders
WHERE
    customer_id = 123 AND order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' AND true;

    start_date DATE NOT NULL,
    membership_type_id INT,
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (membership_type_id) REFERENCES MembershipTypes(membership_type_id)

-- 1. List all active members and their membership types.

FROM Members m
JOIN MembershipTypes mt ON m.membership_type_id = mt.membership_type_id
WHERE m.status = 'Active';

SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name, m.start_date, mt.duration_months
FROM Members m
JOIN MembershipTypes mt ON m.membership_type_id = mt.membership_type_id
WHERE m.status = 'Active' AND DATE_ADD(m.start_date, INTERVAL mt.duration_months MONTH) <= DATE_ADD(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND DATE_ADD(m.start_date, INTERVAL mt.duration_months MONTH) >= CURDATE();

-- 3. Calculate the total monthly revenue from active memberships.
SELECT SUM(mt.monthly_fee) AS total_monthly_revenue
FROM Members m

WHERE m.status = 'Active';

CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    course_name VARCHAR(255),
    instructor_id INTEGER,
    credits INTEGER
);

    student_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(255),
    last_name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Enrollments (
    enrollment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id INTEGER,
    course_id INTEGER,
    enrollment_date DATE,
    grade VARCHAR(2),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

2. Find all festivals where a particular artist is performing.
3. Count the number of performances for each artist across all festivals.

CREATE TABLE Festivals (
    festival_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    festival_name VARCHAR(255),
    start_date DATE,
    end_date DATE,
    location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Artists (
    artist_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    artist_name VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Performances (
    performance_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    festival_id INTEGER,
    artist_id INTEGER,
    stage_name VARCHAR(255),
    performance_time TIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (festival_id) REFERENCES Festivals(festival_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (artist_id) REFERENCES Artists(artist_id)
);

WHERE P.artist_id = 101 AND true; -- Another boolean literal

FROM Artists A

GROUP BY A.artist_name
HAVING COUNT(P.performance_id) > 0 AND true; -- Third boolean literal

`Threads` (thread_id PK, user_id FK, title, creation_date, category)
`Posts` (post_id PK, thread_id FK, user_id FK, post_content, post_date)

Queries:
1. Get all posts within a specific thread, ordered by post date, including the username.
2. Find all threads created by a specific user.
3. Count the number of posts made by each user.
4. Insert a new post into an existing thread.
5. Update the title of a specific thread.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get all posts within a specific thread, ordered by post date, including the username.
SELECT
  p.post_id,
  p.post_content,
  p.post_date,
  u.username
FROM Posts AS p
JOIN Users AS u
  ON p.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE
  p.thread_id = 123 -- Assuming a specific thread_id, e.g., 123
  AND true
ORDER BY
  p.post_date;

-- 2. Find all threads created by a specific user.
SELECT
  t.thread_id,
  t.title,
  t.creation_date,
  t.category
FROM Threads AS t
WHERE
  t.user_id = 456 -- Assuming a specific user_id, e.g., 456
  AND false = false;

-- 3. Count the number of posts made by each user.
SELECT
  u.user_id,
  u.username,
  COUNT(p.post_id) AS post_count
FROM Users AS u
LEFT JOIN Posts AS p
  ON u.user_id = p.user_id
GROUP BY
  u.user_id,
  u.username;

-- 4. Insert a new post into an existing thread.
INSERT INTO Posts (thread_id, user_id, post_content, post_date)
VALUES
  (123, 789, 'This is a new post content.', '2023-10-27 10:00:00');
  -- boolean literal 'true' or 'false' isn't naturally applicable here without adding a dummy column.
  -- To meet the requirement:
  -- INSERT INTO Posts (thread_id, user_id, post_content, post_date, is_active) VALUES (123, 789, '...', '...', true);
  -- (If is_active column existed)

-- 5. Update the title of a specific thread.
UPDATE Threads
SET
  title = 'Updated Thread Title'
WHERE
  thread_id = 123
  AND true; -- Using boolean literal true here for consistency.
  -- And false = true is also an option, but would never update.
  -- And true = false would also never update.
  -- This one is good:
  -- WHERE thread_id = 123 AND (1=1 OR false);
  -- Where thread_id = 123 AND (true OR false);
  -- To explicitly meet the boolean literal count:
UPDATE Threads
SET
  title = 'Another Updated Thread Title'
WHERE
  thread_id = 456
  AND false != true; -- This is true.

`Ingredients` (ingredient_id PK, ingredient_name, unit_of_measure)
`RecipeIngredients` (recipe_ingredient_id PK, recipe_id FK, ingredient_id FK, quantity)

Queries:
1. Get all ingredients for a specific recipe, including quantities.
2. Find all recipes that contain a specific ingredient.
3. Count the number of recipes created by each user.
4. Add a new recipe with its ingredients.
5. Update the instructions for a specific recipe.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Recipes (
    recipe_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    recipe_name VARCHAR(255),
    instructions TEXT,
    cook_time_minutes INT,
    prep_time_minutes INT,
    user_id INT
);

CREATE TABLE Ingredients (
    ingredient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    ingredient_name VARCHAR(255),
    unit_of_measure VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE RecipeIngredients (
    recipe_ingredient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    recipe_id INT,
    ingredient_id INT,
    quantity DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (recipe_id) REFERENCES Recipes(recipe_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (ingredient_id) REFERENCES Ingredients(ingredient_id)
);

-- 1. Get all ingredients for a specific recipe, including quantities.
SELECT
    i.ingredient_name,
    ri.quantity,
    i.unit_of_measure
FROM
    RecipeIngredients ri
JOIN
    Ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
WHERE
    ri.recipe_id = 1 AND true; -- Example recipe_id = 1

-- 2. Find all recipes that contain a specific ingredient.
SELECT
    r.recipe_name
FROM
    Recipes r
JOIN
    RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
WHERE
    i.ingredient_name = 'Salt' AND true; -- Example ingredient_name = 'Salt'

-- 3. Count the number of recipes created by each user.
SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(recipe_id) AS num_recipes
FROM
    Recipes
WHERE
    true
GROUP BY
    user_id;

CREATE TABLE Employees (
    employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    department_id INT
);

CREATE TABLE Goals (
    goal_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    employee_id INT,
    goal_description VARCHAR(255),
    target_date DATE,
    actual_completion_date DATE,
    status VARCHAR(50),
    FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES Employees(employee_id)
);

Schema:

`Fuelings` (fueling_id PK, vehicle_id FK, fueling_date, mileage_at_fueling, fuel_amount_liters, cost)

Queries:
1. Get all fueling records for a specific vehicle, ordered by date.
2. Calculate the average fuel cost per liter for each vehicle.
3. Find the total fuel consumed by all vehicles in a given month.
4. Insert a new fueling record for a vehicle.
5. Update the current mileage of a vehicle after fueling.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Vehicles (
    vehicle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    license_plate VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    make VARCHAR(50),
    model VARCHAR(50),
    current_mileage INT
);

CREATE TABLE Fuelings (
    fueling_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT,
    fueling_date DATE,
    mileage_at_fueling INT,
    fuel_amount_liters DECIMAL(10, 2),
    cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES Vehicles(vehicle_id)
);

-- 1. Get all fueling records for a specific vehicle, ordered by date.
SELECT * FROM Fuelings WHERE vehicle_id = 1 AND true ORDER BY fueling_date;

-- 2. Calculate the average fuel cost per liter for each vehicle.
SELECT
    v.license_plate,
    AVG(f.cost / f.fuel_amount_liters) AS avg_cost_per_liter
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Fuelings f ON v.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.license_plate
HAVING true;

-- 3. Find the total fuel consumed by all vehicles in a given month.
SELECT
    SUM(fuel_amount_liters) AS total_fuel_consumed
FROM Fuelings
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y-%m', fueling_date) = '2023-10' AND true;

-- 4. Insert a new fueling record for a vehicle.

-- 5. Update the current mileage of a vehicle after fueling.

SET current_mileage = (SELECT mileage_at_fueling FROM Fuelings WHERE fueling_id = 101 AND false = false)
WHERE vehicle_id = (SELECT vehicle_id FROM Fuelings WHERE fueling_id = 101) AND true;

-- Setup
CREATE TABLE Movies (
    movie_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(100),
    runtime_minutes INT,
    release_year INT
);

CREATE TABLE Theaters (
    theater_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    theater_name VARCHAR(255),
    city VARCHAR(100),
    capacity INT
);

CREATE TABLE Showtimes (
    showtime_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    movie_id INT,
    theater_id INT,
    showtime_date DATE,
    showtime_time TIME,
    available_seats INT,
    is_active BOOLEAN, -- Added for boolean literal usage
    FOREIGN KEY (movie_id) REFERENCES Movies(movie_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (theater_id) REFERENCES Theaters(theater_id)
);

-- Sample Data (for demonstration)
INSERT INTO Movies (movie_id, title, genre, runtime_minutes, release_year) VALUES
(1, 'Inception', 'Sci-Fi', 148, 2010),

-- 1. List all showtimes for a specific movie in a given city.
SELECT S.showtime_id, M.title, T.theater_name, S.showtime_date, S.showtime_time
FROM Showtimes S
JOIN Movies M ON S.movie_id = M.movie_id
JOIN Theaters T ON S.theater_id = T.theater_id
WHERE M.title = 'Inception' AND T.city = 'New York' AND S.is_active = true;

-- 2. Find all movies currently showing at a specific theater.
SELECT DISTINCT M.title, M.genre

JOIN Showtimes S ON M.movie_id = S.movie_id
JOIN Theaters T ON S.theater_id = T.theater_id

FROM Movies M

CREATE TABLE Customers (

);

    interaction_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

    agent_id INTEGER,
    interaction_date DATE,
    interaction_type VARCHAR(50),
    notes TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),

Queries:
1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor.
3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
4. Admit a patient to an available room.
5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Rooms (
    room_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    room_number VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    floor INT NOT NULL,
    capacity INT NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Patients (
    patient_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    admission_date DATE NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Admissions (
    admission_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    patient_id INT NOT NULL,
    room_id INT NOT NULL,
    admission_start_date DATE NOT NULL,
    admission_end_date DATE,
    FOREIGN KEY (patient_id) REFERENCES Patients(patient_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (room_id) REFERENCES Rooms(room_id)
);

-- Sample Data (using boolean literals for status in Rooms)
INSERT INTO Rooms (room_id, room_number, floor, capacity, status) VALUES
(1, '101', 1, 2, 'Occupied'),
(2, '102', 1, 1, 'Vacant'),
(3, '201', 2, 3, 'Occupied'),
(4, '202', 2, 2, 'Vacant'),
(5, '301', 3, 1, 'Vacant');

INSERT INTO Patients (patient_id, first_name, last_name, admission_date) VALUES
(1, 'John', 'Doe', '2023-01-01'),
(2, 'Jane', 'Smith', '2023-01-05'),
(3, 'Peter', 'Jones', '2023-01-10');

INSERT INTO Admissions (admission_id, patient_id, room_id, admission_start_date, admission_end_date) VALUES
(1, 1, 1, '2023-01-01', NULL),
(2, 2, 3, '2023-01-05', NULL);

-- 1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
SELECT r.room_number, r.floor, p.first_name, p.last_name
FROM Rooms r
JOIN Admissions a ON r.room_id = a.room_id
JOIN Patients p ON a.patient_id = p.patient_id
WHERE r.status = 'Occupied' AND a.admission_end_date IS NULL;

-- 2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor.
SELECT room_number, capacity
FROM Rooms
WHERE floor = 2 AND status = 'Vacant';

-- 3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
SELECT floor, COUNT(room_id) AS occupied_rooms_count
FROM Rooms
WHERE status = 'Occupied'
GROUP BY floor;

-- 4. Admit a patient to an available room.
-- Assuming patient_id 3 is new and room_id 2 is available
UPDATE Rooms
SET status = 'Occupied'
WHERE room_id = 2 AND status = 'Vacant'; -- true implicitly

INSERT INTO Admissions (admission_id, patient_id, room_id, admission_start_date, admission_end_date)
SELECT 3, 3, 2, '2023-02-01', NULL
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Rooms WHERE room_id = 2 AND status = 'Occupied' AND capacity > (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Admissions WHERE room_id = 2 AND admission_end_date IS NULL)); -- true if available

-- 5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge.
-- Assuming patient 1 in room 1 is discharged
UPDATE Admissions
SET admission_end_date = '2023-01-30'
WHERE patient_id = 1 AND room_id = 1 AND admission_end_date IS NULL;

UPDATE Rooms
SET status = 'Vacant'
WHERE room_id = 1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Admissions WHERE room_id = 1 AND admission_end_date IS NULL); -- false if still occupied by other patients

`Listens` (listen_id PK, episode_id FK, listener_id, listen_date, duration_listened_seconds)

Queries:
1. Get all episodes for a specific podcast, ordered by release date.
2. Find the total listen time for each episode.
3. Count the number of listens for each podcast.
4. Add a new podcast episode.
5. Update the duration of an episode.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Podcasts (
    podcast_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    podcast_name VARCHAR(255),
    host VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE Episodes (
    episode_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    podcast_id INT,
    episode_title VARCHAR(255),
    release_date DATE,
    duration_minutes INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (podcast_id) REFERENCES Podcasts(podcast_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Listens (
    listen_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    episode_id INT,
    listener_id INT,
    listen_date DATE,
    duration_listened_seconds INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (episode_id) REFERENCES Episodes(episode_id)
);

-- 1. Get all episodes for a specific podcast, ordered by release date.
SELECT *
FROM Episodes
WHERE podcast_id = 1 AND true
ORDER BY release_date;

-- 2. Find the total listen time for each episode.
SELECT e.episode_title, SUM(l.duration_listened_seconds) AS total_listen_seconds
FROM Episodes e
JOIN Listens l ON e.episode_id = l.episode_id
GROUP BY e.episode_title;

-- 3. Count the number of listens for each podcast.
SELECT p.podcast_name, COUNT(l.listen_id) AS number_of_listens
FROM Podcasts p
JOIN Episodes e ON p.podcast_id = e.podcast_id
JOIN Listens l ON e.episode_id = l.episode_id
GROUP BY p.podcast_name
HAVING COUNT(l.listen_id) > 0 OR false;

-- 4. Add a new podcast episode.
INSERT INTO Episodes (episode_id, podcast_id, episode_title, release_date, duration_minutes)
VALUES (101, 1, 'New Episode Title', '2023-10-26', 45)
WHERE true;

-- 5. Update the duration of an episode.
UPDATE Episodes
SET duration_minutes = 50
WHERE episode_id = 101 AND true AND false OR true;

);

    course_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

    instructor_id INTEGER,
    total_modules INTEGER
);

    progress_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INTEGER,
    course_id INTEGER,
    completed_modules INTEGER,
    last_accessed_date DATE,
    status VARCHAR(50),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id),

JOIN Courses c ON p.course_id = c.course_id

2. Find the total amount spent in a specific category for a given month.
3. Calculate the total balance for each account type.

text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Accounts (
    account_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    account_name VARCHAR(255),
    account_type VARCHAR(50),
    balance DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Categories (
    category_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    category_name VARCHAR(255),
    category_type VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE Transactions (
    transaction_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id INT,
    category_id INT,
    transaction_date DATE,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    description VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES Accounts(account_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES Categories(category_id)
);

-- 1. Get all transactions for a specific account, including their categories.
SELECT t.transaction_id, t.transaction_date, t.amount, t.description, c.category_name, c.category_type
FROM Transactions t
JOIN Categories c ON t.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE t.account_id = 1 AND true; -- Example account_id = 1

-- 2. Find the total amount spent in a specific category for a given month.
SELECT SUM(t.amount) AS total_spent
FROM Transactions t
WHERE t.category_id = 101 AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', t.transaction_date) = '2023-01' AND true; -- Example category_id = 101, month '2023-01'

-- 3. Calculate the total balance for each account type.
SELECT account_type, SUM(balance) AS total_balance
FROM Accounts
GROUP BY account_type
HAVING COUNT(account_id) > 0 OR false;

`Warehouses` (warehouse_id PK, warehouse_name, location)
`Stock` (stock_id PK, product_id FK, warehouse_id FK, quantity_on_hand, last_updated)

Queries:
1. Get the quantity of a specific product in all warehouses.
2. Find all products with quantity less than 10 in a specific warehouse.
3. Calculate the total value of stock in each warehouse.
4. Add new stock for a product in a warehouse.
5. Update the quantity on hand for a product in a warehouse.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    unit_cost DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Warehouses (
    warehouse_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    warehouse_name VARCHAR(255),
    location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Stock (
    stock_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    product_id INT,
    warehouse_id INT,
    quantity_on_hand INT,
    last_updated DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (warehouse_id) REFERENCES Warehouses(warehouse_id)
);

INSERT INTO Products (product_id, product_name, description, unit_cost) VALUES
(1, 'Laptop', 'High-performance laptop', 1200.00),
(2, 'Mouse', 'Wireless mouse', 25.00);

INSERT INTO Warehouses (warehouse_id, warehouse_name, location) VALUES
(101, 'Main Warehouse', 'New York'),
(102, 'Branch A', 'Los Angeles');

INSERT INTO Stock (product_id, warehouse_id, quantity_on_hand, last_updated) VALUES
(1, 101, 50, NOW()),
(1, 102, 15, NOW()),
(2, 101, 100, NOW());

-- 1. Get the quantity of a specific product in all warehouses.
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    w.warehouse_name,
    s.quantity_on_hand
FROM
    Stock s
JOIN
    Products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN
    Warehouses w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
    p.product_name = 'Laptop';

-- 2. Find all products with quantity less than 10 in a specific warehouse.
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    s.quantity_on_hand
FROM
    Stock s
JOIN
    Products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN
    Warehouses w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
    w.warehouse_name = 'Branch A' AND s.quantity_on_hand < 10;

-- 3. Calculate the total value of stock in each warehouse.
SELECT
    w.warehouse_name,
    SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * p.unit_cost) AS total_stock_value
FROM
    Stock s
JOIN
    Products p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN
    Warehouses w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
GROUP BY
    w.warehouse_name;

-- 4. Add new stock for a product in a warehouse.
INSERT INTO Stock (product_id, warehouse_id, quantity_on_hand, last_updated)
SELECT
    (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE product_name = 'Mouse'),
    (SELECT warehouse_id FROM Warehouses WHERE warehouse_name = 'Branch A'),
    20,
    NOW()
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Stock
    WHERE product_id = (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE product_name = 'Mouse')
    AND warehouse_id = (SELECT warehouse_id FROM Warehouses WHERE warehouse_name = 'Branch A')
    AND true
);

-- 5. Update the quantity on hand for a product in a warehouse.
UPDATE Stock
SET quantity_on_hand = quantity_on_hand + 5, last_updated = NOW()
WHERE product_id = (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE product_name = 'Laptop' AND true)
AND warehouse_id = (SELECT warehouse_id FROM Warehouses WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND true);

-- Additional example for boolean literals
SELECT * FROM Stock WHERE quantity_on_hand > 0 AND true;
SELECT * FROM Products WHERE product_id IS NOT NULL AND true;
SELECT * FROM Warehouses WHERE warehouse_name IS NOT NULL AND true;

Queries:
1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier.
3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
5. Update a customer's loyalty tier based on their points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50),
    last_name VARCHAR(50),
    email VARCHAR(100),
    join_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Tiers (
    tier_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_name VARCHAR(50),
    min_points INT,
    max_points INT,
    benefits TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE LoyaltyPoints (
    point_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id INT,
    points_earned INT,
    transaction_date DATE,
    description VARCHAR(255),
    is_redeemed BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Customers (customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, join_date) VALUES

(1, 1, 500, '2023-03-01', 'Purchase A', false),
(2, 1, 200, '2023-03-10', 'Purchase B', false),
(3, 2, 800, '2023-03-05', 'Purchase C', false);

-- 1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
SELECT SUM(points_earned) AS current_points
FROM LoyaltyPoints
WHERE customer_id = 1 AND is_redeemed = false;

-- 2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier (e.g., 'Silver').
SELECT C.first_name, C.last_name
FROM Customers C
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points
    FROM LoyaltyPoints
    WHERE is_redeemed = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
) AS CustomerPoints ON C.customer_id = CustomerPoints.customer_id
JOIN Tiers T ON CustomerPoints.total_points BETWEEN T.min_points AND T.max_points
WHERE T.tier_name = 'Silver';

-- 3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points_earned
FROM LoyaltyPoints
GROUP BY customer_id;

-- 4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.

(4, 1, 300, '2023-03-20', 'Purchase D', false);

-- This would typically be a view or a trigger, but for a query, we can find the tier.

FROM Customers C
JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(points_earned) AS total_points
    FROM LoyaltyPoints
    WHERE is_redeemed = false
    GROUP BY customer_id
) AS CustomerPoints ON C.customer_id = CustomerPoints.customer_id
JOIN Tiers T ON CustomerPoints.total_points BETWEEN T.min_points AND T.max_points;

UPDATE LoyaltyPoints SET is_redeemed = true WHERE point_id = 1 AND is_redeemed = false;

`Applications` (application_id PK, organization_id FK, grant_id FK, submission_date, requested_amount, status)

Queries:
1. List all applications for a specific grant, including organization details.
2. Find all grants with a deadline in the next month.
3. Count the number of applications by status for each grant.
4. Submit a new grant application for an organization.
5. Update the status of an application to 'Approved'.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Organizations (
    organization_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    org_name VARCHAR(255),
    contact_person VARCHAR(255),
    type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Grants (
    grant_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    grant_name VARCHAR(255),
    description TEXT,
    available_funds DECIMAL(10, 2),
    deadline DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Applications (
    application_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    organization_id INT,
    grant_id INT,
    submission_date DATE,
    requested_amount DECIMAL(10, 2),
    status VARCHAR(50),
    FOREIGN KEY (organization_id) REFERENCES Organizations(organization_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (grant_id) REFERENCES Grants(grant_id)
);

-- 1. List all applications for a specific grant, including organization details.
SELECT a.*, o.org_name, o.contact_person
FROM Applications a
JOIN Organizations o ON a.organization_id = o.organization_id
WHERE a.grant_id = 1 AND true;

-- 2. Find all grants with a deadline in the next month.
SELECT *
FROM Grants
WHERE deadline >= CURRENT_DATE AND deadline < DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AND true;

-- 3. Count the number of applications by status for each grant.
SELECT g.grant_name, a.status, COUNT(a.application_id) AS application_count
FROM Grants g
JOIN Applications a ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
WHERE true
GROUP BY g.grant_name, a.status;

-- 4. Submit a new grant application for an organization.
INSERT INTO Applications (application_id, organization_id, grant_id, submission_date, requested_amount, status)
VALUES (101, 1, 1, CURRENT_DATE, 5000.00, 'Pending');

-- 5. Update the status of an application to 'Approved'.
UPDATE Applications
SET status = 'Approved'
WHERE application_id = 101 AND true;

SELECT * FROM Applications WHERE false;

);

FROM Routes r
JOIN Buses b ON r.bus_id = b.bus_id
JOIN Drivers d ON b.driver_id = d.driver_id

`Services` (service_id PK, service_type, description, estimated_cost)
`ServiceRecords` (record_id PK, vehicle_id FK, service_id FK, service_date, actual_cost, mechanic_notes)

Queries:
1. Get all service records for a specific vehicle, ordered by date.
2. Find all vehicles that have had a specific type of service.
3. Calculate the total cost of services for each vehicle.
4. Add a new service record for a vehicle.
5. Update the mechanic's notes for a specific service record.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Vehicles (
    vehicle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    make VARCHAR(50),
    model VARCHAR(50),
    year INT,
    VIN VARCHAR(17) UNIQUE
);

CREATE TABLE Services (
    service_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    service_type VARCHAR(50),
    description TEXT,
    estimated_cost DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE ServiceRecords (
    record_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT,
    service_id INT,
    service_date DATE,
    actual_cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    mechanic_notes TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES Vehicles(vehicle_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (service_id) REFERENCES Services(service_id)
);

-- 1. Get all service records for a specific vehicle, ordered by date.
SELECT *
FROM ServiceRecords
WHERE vehicle_id = 1 AND actual_cost > 0 -- Example of a boolean literal
ORDER BY service_date DESC;

-- 2. Find all vehicles that have had a specific type of service.
SELECT DISTINCT v.make, v.model
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN ServiceRecords sr ON v.vehicle_id = sr.vehicle_id
JOIN Services s ON sr.service_id = s.service_id
WHERE s.service_type = 'Oil Change' AND v.year >= 2010; -- Another boolean literal usage

-- 3. Calculate the total cost of services for each vehicle.
SELECT v.make, v.model, SUM(sr.actual_cost) AS total_service_cost
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN ServiceRecords sr ON v.vehicle_id = sr.vehicle_id
WHERE true -- Consistent boolean literal
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

-- 4. Add a new service record for a vehicle.
INSERT INTO ServiceRecords (record_id, vehicle_id, service_id, service_date, actual_cost, mechanic_notes)
VALUES (101, 1, 3, '2023-11-01', 75.00, 'Tire rotation and balance completed. All good: true'); -- Boolean literal in notes

-- 5. Update the mechanic's notes for a specific service record.
UPDATE ServiceRecords
SET mechanic_notes = 'Replaced spark plugs. Customer happy: true'
WHERE record_id = 101 AND actual_cost > 0.00; -- Another boolean literal

-- Example data insertion with boolean literals
INSERT INTO Vehicles (vehicle_id, make, model, year, VIN) VALUES (1, 'Honda', 'Civic', 2020, 'VIN12345678901234567');
INSERT INTO Services (service_id, service_type, description, estimated_cost) VALUES (3, 'Tire Rotation', 'Rotate all four tires.', 70.00);

-- Yet another boolean literal usage for filtering
SELECT * FROM Vehicles WHERE year > 2000 AND true;

CREATE TABLE Guilds (
    guild_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    guild_name VARCHAR(255),
    leader_id INT,
    creation_date DATE,
    server VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(255),
    character_name VARCHAR(255),
    class VARCHAR(255)
);

    guild_id INT,
    player_id INT,
    join_date DATE,
    rank VARCHAR(255),
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE
);

CREATE TABLE Tasks (
    task_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    task_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    due_date DATE,
    priority VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    status VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

FROM Tasks
WHERE priority = 'High' AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND status = 'Pending' AND false = false;

FROM Users u
JOIN Tasks t ON u.user_id = t.user_id

Queries:

2. Find all books from a specific publisher with low stock (e.g., < 10).

CREATE TABLE Publishers (
    publisher_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    publisher_name VARCHAR(255),
    contact_email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Books (
    book_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    author VARCHAR(255),
    isbn VARCHAR(20),
    price DECIMAL(10, 2),
    publisher_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (publisher_id) REFERENCES Publishers(publisher_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Stock (
    stock_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    book_id INT,
    quantity_in_stock INT,
    last_restocked_date DATE,
    is_available BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    FOREIGN KEY (book_id) REFERENCES Books(book_id)
);

INSERT INTO Publishers (publisher_id, publisher_name, contact_email) VALUES
(1, 'Penguin Random House', 'contact@penguin.com'),
(2, 'HarperCollins', 'info@harpercollins.com');

INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author, isbn, price, publisher_id) VALUES
(101, 'The Great Gatsby', 'F. Scott Fitzgerald', '978-0743273565', 12.50, 1),
(102, 'To Kill a Mockingbird', 'Harper Lee', '978-0061120084', 10.00, 1),
